\ednentry{
  id = {EDN-77},
  title = {The raw frame's measured fill rates are asserted by the Great Expectations suites, not promised by the raw contract},
  date = {2026-10-06},
  milestone = {M3: Quality Assurance},
  topic = {Data Quality, Data Validation},
  participants = {@lukas2510, decided by the repository owner},
  decision = {\texttt{make}, \texttt{body\_\allowbreak{}type} and the four \texttt{equipment\_\allowbreak{}*} lists are nullable in \texttt{RAW\_\allowbreak{}SCHEMA}, as they already were in \texttt{INTERIM\_\allowbreak{}SCHEMA}, so the contracts hold only structural nullability.
Both Great Expectations suites assert those six columns filled up to one tolerance, \texttt{validate.\allowbreak{}required\_\allowbreak{}filled\_\allowbreak{}mostly: 0.\allowbreak{}999}, in \texttt{params.\allowbreak{}yaml}.
The interim rule, which was hard, becomes the same tolerant rule.},
  rationale = {\emph{Alternatives considered:}
\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=*, topsep=2pt]
\item \textbf{Option A (chosen): nullable in the raw contract, tolerant fill-rate rule in both suites, one shared tolerance.}
\newline Pros: a gap in a scrape is reported by \texttt{validate-\allowbreak{}data} as a data-quality finding, with the rule named and the row count, instead of as a contract error in \texttt{download} that reads like a bug in our code; the raw contract keeps only what the file is structurally; one semantics on both frames, so a gap the raw suite tolerates does not then fail the interim suite.
\newline Cons: a tolerated gap travels through \texttt{preprocess} as a null, which the interim contract already allowed; the interim rule no longer fails on a single value that preprocessing empties, only past 0.1\,\% of the rows.
\item \textbf{Option B: keep the raw contract as it is and correct the wording only.}
\newline Pros: no code change and no risk to the pipeline.
\newline Cons: the pipeline stops in the wrong stage with the wrong kind of message, and the fill-rate rule keeps documenting a path no scrape can reach.
\item \textbf{Option C: tolerant on raw, the interim rule stays hard.}
\newline Pros: catches every value preprocessing empties.
\newline Cons: contradicts the raw rule, because a gap the raw suite tolerates would then fail the interim suite, so the tolerance would never take effect.
\item \textbf{Option D: tolerant on raw, a separate and stricter tolerance on interim.}
\newline Pros: mirrors the two roles of the frames.
\newline Cons: a second parameter for a distinction that nothing in the data currently needs.
\end{itemize}
\par
\emph{Why:} A contract answers ``is this our bug'', a suite answers ``did the data change'', and a fill rate is the second kind of question.
The raw contract answered it on the data's behalf, because the snapshot happens to fill these columns in every row, so the first gap in a future scrape would have stopped the pipeline in \texttt{download} and never reached the rule written for it.
Option A makes both frames say the same thing.
The tolerance of 0.999 follows \texttt{mileage\_\allowbreak{}mostly}: far tighter than the 0.99 of \texttt{filled\_\allowbreak{}mostly}, because these columns are filled in 100\,\% of the snapshot, yet it tolerates a few gaps as a finding and still fails a scrape that has lost a column.},
  ai = {Information seeking, Alternative generation, Alternative assessment, Recommendation, Solution generation},
  response = {Accepted},
  assessment = {AI read the contract, both suites and every consumer of the raw frame, generated options A to D with their pros and cons, recommended A with the 0.999 tolerance, and implemented it with tests that fail on a missing \texttt{body\_\allowbreak{}type} through \texttt{download}'s contract and through the \texttt{validate-\allowbreak{}data} stage.
Lukas chose A as recommended and asked for the decision to be recorded.
Issue \#78 had already named the problem and the two open questions, the tolerance and the fate of the interim rule, which the options settle.},
  aievidence = {Claude Code session of 2026-10-06: the options were put to Lukas with a recommendation before any code changed, and he chose ``1A + 2A with 0.999'' and asked for an EDN entry.},
  evidence = {\href{https://github.com/mlops-2627q1-mds-upc/MLOPS_Recommenditos/issues/78}{issue \#78}, found in the review of \href{https://github.com/mlops-2627q1-mds-upc/MLOPS_Recommenditos/pull/76}{\#76}; \href{https://github.com/mlops-2627q1-mds-upc/MLOPS_Recommenditos/blob/main/recommenditos/schema.py}{\texttt{recommenditos/\allowbreak{}schema.\allowbreak{}py}}; \href{https://github.com/mlops-2627q1-mds-upc/MLOPS_Recommenditos/blob/main/recommenditos/data/gx_context_configuration.py}{\texttt{recommenditos/\allowbreak{}data/\allowbreak{}gx\_\allowbreak{}context\_\allowbreak{}configuration.\allowbreak{}py}}, \texttt{REQUIRED\_\allowbreak{}FILLED\_\allowbreak{}COLUMNS}; \href{https://github.com/mlops-2627q1-mds-upc/MLOPS_Recommenditos/blob/main/tests/test_validate_data.py}{\texttt{tests/\allowbreak{}test\_\allowbreak{}validate\_\allowbreak{}data.\allowbreak{}py}}; \href{https://github.com/mlops-2627q1-mds-upc/MLOPS_Recommenditos/blob/main/docs/docs/pipeline.md}{pipeline docs}, Data validation; EDN-68 is the entry for \#25, whose suites this changes.},
